name: Max-cut, G-set G8
description: Partition the 800 vertices of the G-set graph G8 into two sides so that the total weight of the edges whose endpoints are on different sides is as large as possible (max-cut). The graph is undirected and has 19176 edges, each given once; every edge has weight 1 or -1, and an edge of weight -1 that is cut lowers the total.
contract: solve(n, edges) -> sequence of n integers, each 0 or 1: the side of every vertex. edges is an int64 array with one row (i, j, w) per edge, vertices numbered from 0. Score: total weight of the edges whose endpoints are on different sides, maximized.
notes: The best-known cut was not read for this instance; check the G-set literature before claiming a record.

G-set graph G8: a sparse random graph of density 6 percent (800 vertices, 19176 edges, weights +1 and -1, average degree 47.9); the weight of a cut is the sum of the weights of edges whose endpoints lie on different sides.
Specialised solvers (breakout local search, simulated bifurcation, GES-PR) are strong on this set.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find a partition of the vertices of the G-set graph G8 into two sides that maximises the total weight of the edges between the sides (max-cut).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Max-cut asks for the heaviest cut of a weighted graph and is NP-hard. It is equivalent to finding a ground state of an Ising spin glass without external field, and it models via minimisation in circuit layout; its semidefinite relaxation gave one of the best-known approximation algorithms. The G-set graphs (800 to 20,000 vertices) have been a standard test bed for heuristics and Ising machines for about 25 years, and for the large sparse graphs a better cut is a better solution of an open or unproven instance.

papers.primary_goal: Reduce spin-glass ground states and via minimisation in circuit layout to max-cut and solve the resulting instances with a cutting-plane algorithm.

papers.primary_goal: Give a randomised approximation algorithm for max-cut based on a semidefinite programming relaxation.

papers.title: Rank-Two Relaxation Heuristics for MAX-CUT and Other Binary Quadratic Programs

papers.primary_goal: Develop fast rank-two relaxation heuristics for large max-cut instances and compare them with semidefinite programming codes.
